page.layout: Two printed pages on the scan. Left page: running head at top, then main text in one column, a woodcut initial, and a chapter heading. Right page: only the edge of a neighbouring column of text is visible at the right margin, which is not transcribed. No marginal notes on the left page.

main_text.p: teris notis ἐν ῳ σίχῳ locatis, gradibusq; ὑπερβάσις ἀπλάσι & καπνάσι& observatur.
Periodus est comprehensio graduum: Perfecta quidē quæ tribus: Imperfecta, quæ paucioribus constat.
Quæ denique uno graduum ternario conficitur, Simplex: quæ uerò multiplici, Composita existit.

p.i: In numeris sic se gradus ad periodos habent, sicut in Oratione cōmata, uel cola ad easdem. Perfectæ periodi sunt, ut 123 simplex, 123456 duplex seu composita. Imperfectæ, ut 12 simplex, 1234, 12345 duplices. 12345678 triplex: compositæ omnes.

main_text.head: CAPVT III.
De altera Notationis parte.
main_text.p: VCVSQVE notationis generale fuit προσωαύδμα: sequitur pars altera, quę dati cuiuslibet numeri scripturam specialiter explicat.
Atq; hîc numeri occurrunt uel unius termini, uel plurium. Uno termino scribuntur integra.

p.i: Vt 360, 1578, &c. numeri μονόσοιχοι, quasi una serie & acie descripti.

page.notes: The woodcut initial H is set in a decorative frame. The first Greek line and the Greek word in the Caput III paragraph are printed in Greek; some Greek is uncertain and may contain errors. The word "Inte-" at the foot is a catchword-like hyphenated start of the next page. The right page shows only fragments of the neighbouring column (ter, ex, ue, to, en, cu, lie, pro, tur, enu, tum, finer, nulli, milli, riod, quen, dis, rum, nem, stror, dum, quat, ginta), which are not transcribed.
